about: Source plan for higher-resolution relief (land) and bathymetry (sea) per region. Read by scripts/build_hires.py and docs/hires-sources.md. Nothing in this file has been downloaded: 'status' records how far each source was checked. verified = the endpoint answered a metadata or HEAD request on the research date; documented = described by the provider but not called; unverified = could not be confirmed (script refuses it unless --include-unverified); manual = no public API found, drop the file in data/raw/<region>/manual/<source id>/.

limits.note: The elevation texture the browser draws from must stay under about 8,192 px a side and about 10 MB as lossless 16-bit WebP (Vestland: 0.9 byte per pixel). That caps the web cell of a whole-region example at 250 to 600 m whatever the source resolution; finer sources only pay off with a tiled, zoomable delivery (see docs/hires-sources.md, 'What resolution can the page show').

style.name: Detuned
style.relief: stepped (non-linear classes, cross-blended by climate zone)

cop_glo90.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90
cop_glo90.attribution: © DLR e.V. 2010–2014 and © Airbus 2014–2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
cop_glo90.note: Current land source (fetch_region.py). Heights on EGM2008.

cop_glo30.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
cop_glo30.licence: Copernicus (free for the general public; the AWS readme links an older annex, check the current one)
cop_glo30.attribution: © DLR e.V. 2010–2014 and © Airbus 2014–2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
cop_glo30.note: 3x finer than GLO-90 everywhere. COG with internal overviews: reading at a 300 m cell transfers about 1/100 of the tile. Tile URL checked 2026-11-08 (N60 E010). Some countries' tiles are withheld; the script falls back to GLO-90.

arcticdem_32m.name: ArcticDEM mosaic v4.1, 32 m
arcticdem_32m.attribution: ArcticDEM (Porter et al.), Polar Geospatial Center, University of Minnesota; accessed {date} from https://registry.opendata.aws/pgc-arcticdem
arcticdem_32m.note: Covers land north of about 60 N: Svalbard, Kola, Novaya Zemlya, Franz Josef Land, northern Norway. Index VRT and 32 m and 10 m tiles listed on the open bucket. Fills voids in GLO-30/90 at high latitude but is a surface model (trees, ice): use only where GLO is weak.

arcticdem_10m.name: ArcticDEM mosaic v4.1, 10 m
arcticdem_10m.note: Only for zoomed views; far more than a whole-region example can show.

npi_svalbard_dtm20.name: NPI Svalbard DTM 20
npi_svalbard_dtm20.note: Capabilities answered: a single area (the whole archipelago). Built from NPI aerial photogrammetry; better than GLO on the glaciers' edges and fjord coasts. Also Svalbard DTM 5 (010bfb4a-65aa-4d30-aba9-7d090a432df7) and DTM 50 (3a83e0a7-113e-4850-8fed-1646838acb02).

npi_janmayen_dtm5.name: NPI Jan Mayen DTM 5
npi_janmayen_dtm5.note: Jan Mayen is outside every region frame except possibly norwegian_sea's west edge; listed for completeness.

kartverket_dtm_seamless.name: Kartverket national terrain model, seamless WCS
kartverket_dtm_seamless.licence: Norge digitalt-lisens (access limited to Norway Digital partners; Geonorge record 311782b2-26fe-4d1d-93e9-c90b45d5bd8b). NOT open data: do not publish products derived from it.
kartverket_dtm_seamless.note: EXCLUDED from every region (2026-11-08). The service answers without credentials and was used for a first build, but its Geonorge record is 'Norge digitalt begrenset' under the Norge digitalt licence, so tiles derived from it cannot be redistributed. Technical notes for reference: ArcGIS WCS; WCS 1.0.0 width/height resamples server-side; returns exact 0 outside Norway. Open alternatives: GLO-30 (used), or DTM 10 / DTM 1 from hoydedata.no (CC BY 4.0).

kartverket_dtm10_historic.name: Kartverket DTM 10, historic annual version
kartverket_dtm10_historic.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Geonorge record dddbb667...). Data from 2013; the current model is on hoydedata.no.
kartverket_dtm10_historic.note: Capabilities and 146 map-sheet areas answered for UTM 32. Marked 'Historisk': Kartverket says the current model is exported from hoydedata.no. A fallback if the WCS cannot scale. Not scripted: its areas are map sheets (e.g. 6403-1) without published outlines, so choosing sheets for a region needs a manual order on geonorge.no; drop the GeoTIFFs in data/raw/<region>/manual/kartverket_dtm10_historic/.

os_terrain50.name: OS Terrain 50
os_terrain50.licence: OS OpenData, Open Government Licence v3
os_terrain50.attribution: Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right {year}
os_terrain50.note: Listing answered without a key. Great Britain including Shetland and Orkney. Not a GeoTIFF: read the .asc tiles directly.

etopo_2022_60s.name: NOAA ETOPO 2022, 60 arc-second surface
etopo_2022_60s.attribution: NOAA NCEI (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model
etopo_2022_60s.note: Current world and far-Arctic source. Server is slow (about 0.5 MB/s): windows only, sampled for coarse grids.

gebco_2026.name: GEBCO_2026 Grid
gebco_2026.licence: Public domain; acknowledge GEBCO; not for navigation
gebco_2026.attribution: GEBCO Bathymetric Compilation Group 2026 (2026) The GEBCO_2026 Grid. doi:10.5285/4f68d5c7-45eb-f999-e063-7086abc036fa
gebco_2026.note: GEBCO_2026 ice-surface grid, 15 arc-second (463 m at the equator), published April 2026. CEDA serves eight 90 x 90 degree GeoTIFF tiles unzipped (int16, uncompressed, 933 MB each, range requests supported; checked 2026-11-08), so the script reads each tile in bands of full rows, averages to the target cell and keeps only the result: about 5 GB of transfer for the Atlantic, nothing stored. Global zip 4.2 GB and NetCDF 4.2 GB also on CEDA. Used for the Atlantic; not for the world (5 km) or the Barents Sea, where ETOPO and IBCAO already match the cell.

ibcao_v5.name: IBCAO v5.2 (2026), 400 m
ibcao_v5.licence: Open Government Licence v3 (CEDA record 30ad58b6...); cite as given; not for navigation
ibcao_v5.attribution: IBCAO Version 5.2 Compilation Group (2026): The International Bathymetric Chart of the Arctic Ocean (IBCAO) Version 5.2. NERC British Oceanographic Data Centre, accessed {date}. https://catalogue.ceda.ac.uk/uuid/30ad58b60d8c4a4dab6d64a40640540a
ibcao_v5.note: Version 5.2 (2026) is on CEDA at 100, 200 and 400 m. The 100 m grid is a 12 GB zip (200 m: 3 GB), too big for this 10 GB disk and finer than the 300 to 600 m cells drawn, so the 400 m grid (776 MB zip) is streamed, clipped to the region and deleted. The zips are deflated, so no windowed reads: use the 16-tile 100 m zip (also 12 GB) only with more disk. Covers north of about 64 N in polar stereographic (EPSG:3996). Priority: below EMODnet (115 m) wherever EMODnet has data; it fills east of 43 E and north of Svalbard.

emodnet_dtm_2024.name: EMODnet Bathymetry DTM 2024
emodnet_dtm_2024.attribution: EMODnet Bathymetry Consortium (2024): EMODnet Digital Bathymetry (DTM)
emodnet_dtm_2024.note: Current sea source. Covers 11 N to 90 N, 70.5 W to 43 E. WCS scaling is not supported (500 errors) and requests over about 2 degrees are refused. EMODnet also lists 'high-resolution snapshots' at 1/32 to 1/512 arc-minute for some areas: not scripted (areas not published in a form I could read).

kartverket_sea_50.name: Kartverket sea-floor terrain model, 50 m
kartverket_sea_50.note: Already scripted (fetch_kartverket_sea.py). Cells NHS-Drrcc, half a degree each. Agrees with EMODnet to a median of 0 m (EMODnet already contains these surveys): the gain is resolution, not different depths.

kartverket_sea_25.name: Kartverket sea-floor terrain model, 25 m (MAREANO)
kartverket_sea_25.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Geonorge record 39e022aa...); 25 m only outside territorial waters (higher resolution near the coast is classified)
kartverket_sea_25.note: Capabilities answered: 1,085 half-degree cells. Only outside the 12 nm limit and only where MAREANO has surveyed (Møre to Finnmark, the eastern Barents Sea, parts around Svalbard). Overlay on the 50 m model where present.

dk_dybdemodel_50.name: Denmark's Depth Model, 50 m (2024)
dk_dybdemodel_50.licence: Free incl. commercial; not for navigation; the agency may withdraw downloads
dk_dybdemodel_50.attribution: Danmarks Dybdemodel, 50 m opløsning, retrieved {date} (Danish Geodata Agency)
dk_dybdemodel_50.note: Covers the Danish EEZ. GeoTIFF or web service via a free Dataforsyningen account/token. seabed.py already reads data/raw/<region>/denmark_dybdemodel50/.

bsh_dtm_50.name: BSH seabed DTM North Sea and Baltic, 50 m
bsh_dtm_50.licence: Free under GeoZG; no licence name found: confirm on the GeoSeaPortal
bsh_dtm_50.note: German EEZ, 50 m grid via the GeoSeaPortal (no API found). 1 m grids by request, possibly for a fee.

ukho_mdp.name: UKHO ADMIRALTY Marine Data Portal bathymetry
ukho_mdp.licence: UKHO Bathymetry Data Licence (OGL plus a not-for-navigation term)
ukho_mdp.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 and © Crown copyright UKHO
ukho_mdp.note: Over 4,000 survey surfaces; formats found were GeoJSON, KML and Shapefile (outlines) and I could not confirm gridded downloads. Not scriptable yet. EMODnet already composites the UK surveys at 115 m.

north_sea.gain: Norwegian shelf and fjord mouths from 115 m to 25 to 50 m. Land stays Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m) with OS Terrain 50 for Shetland: Kartverket's lidar terrain service is not open data (Norge digitalt licence) and is excluded.

norwegian_sea.gain: MAREANO's 25 m grid over the Norwegian Sea shelf, banks and the Storegga slide area (outside 12 nm), plus Nordland's coast.

barents_sea.gain: The biggest real upgrade: the sea east of 43 E and north of 80 N goes from 1.8 km ETOPO to 100 m IBCAO v5; Svalbard from GLO-90 to NPI 20 m or ArcticDEM 32 m; the Norwegian Barents shelf to MAREANO 25 m.

ne_europe.gain: Modest. At a 600 m cell GLO-30 (30 m) and EMODnet (115 m) are already finer than the picture; national models (Germany DGM, Poland NMT 1 m, Netherlands AHN, Denmark DHM) add nothing visible at this scale and were not scripted. The gain here is cleaner averaging from GLO-30 and the Danish and German 50 m models in their own waters.

world.gain: Replaces ETOPO sampled every fifth cell (1.8 km source, 9 km sample) with GEBCO 2026 averaged properly from 450 m: no aliasing on coasts and ridges. The only new thing needed is the GEBCO download.

vestland.gain: Already uses Kartverket 50 m for the sea (demo page). Land would move from GLO-90 to the national model.

atlantic.gain: Basin scale for spreading ridges: GEBCO 2026 (15 arc-second, about 463 m) averaged to 2 km, replacing ETOPO 2022 (1.85 km source). Deep-ocean GEBCO is largely satellite-altimetry-predicted at a few km, so the gain is sharpest where ships have surveyed (ridge axes, margins, seamounts); fracture zones sharpen modestly.

north_sea_wide.gain: Landscape frame (about 2:1) for wide web pages; same sources as north_sea, coarse grid only, no hires build.

norwegian_sea_wide.gain: Landscape frame (about 2:1) for wide web pages; same sources as norwegian_sea, coarse grid only, no hires build.

ne_europe_wide.gain: Landscape frame (about 2:1) for wide web pages; same sources as ne_europe, coarse grid only, no hires build.
